newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended a quiet day's trading sharply lower but the impact of a sell-off in German bunds was cushioned by a short-squeeze in guilder paper.
Dealers said concern over Russian president Boris Yeltsin's health were among the factors that sparked the tumble in bunds, which dragged down Dutch bonds.
But guilder bonds did not fall by the same extent, widening the yield discount to Germany.
"There's still some shorts in guilders," said one dealer, attributing this to a continuing favourable response to last Tuesday's Dutch national budget.
He noted a short squeeze in Dutch paper maturing between 2002 and 2004 as well as 2007 and 2010 bonds.
Another trader said market players were squaring their books ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee's meeting on Tuesday, which comes amid expectations of a U.S. interest rate hike.
"Everyone is waiting for the FOMC tomorrow," he said, adding that he expected a truer indication of the bond market's direction to come on Wednesday.
One dealer said: "I expect another quiet morning (tomorrow)."
